life_summary: Rudger Judd Clawson was born on March 12, 1857, in Salt Lake City, Utah Territory, the son of Hiram Bradley Clawson and Margaret Judd. He grew up in the heart of the Salt Lake Valley during the formative years of the Utah Territory. As a young man, Clawson developed a deep commitment to missionary work and ecclesiastical service. His missionary experience profoundly shaped his character: in July 1879, while serving in Georgia, his companion Joseph Standing was killed by a mob at Varnell Station, yet Clawson faced the armed mob with composure and conviction, refusing to be intimidated. This early experience of persecution and faithfulness established him as a model of moral courage and steadfast devotion.
church_summary: Rudger Clawson served as a missionary in Georgia and was ordained an apostle on October 10, 1898. He served continuously in the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles for forty-five years until his death in 1943. From 1921 to 1943, he served as President of the Quorum, holding this position for twenty-two years, the second-longest tenure in that office. In 1901, he was briefly called as Second Counselor in the First Presidency under Lorenzo Snow, serving for five days. He was the first polygamist convicted under the Edmunds Act in August 1882, receiving a sentence of three and a half years plus a $1,500 fine. He was pardoned by President Grover Cleveland in 1887. In 1904, the town of Kingsville, Utah, was renamed Clawson in his honor. He died on June 21, 1943, in Salt Lake City, from pneumonia at age 86.
